newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander sells 2.1 mln First Union shares.
newsitem.headline: Santander sells 2.1 mln First Union shares.

text.p: Spain's largest bank Banco Santander said on Thursday that it had sold a further 2.1 million shares of First Union Corp stock in a block trade transaction on the New York Stock Exchange.
This follows a previous sale of 3.6 million shares of First Union on August 7, Santander said in a statement.
"(The sale) is intended to position Santander's stake in the U.S. bank below 10 percent and thereby free up Group capital," Santander said.
Under Bank of International Settlements guidelines, share participations above 10 percent in non-consolidated companies are deducted from total capital.
The sale releases 57 billion pesetas in capital, it said.

Originally, the stock sale in August left Santander with less than 10 percent of First Union. But a subsequent decrease in the number of First Union's outstanding shares left Santander with 10.42 percent at the end of September.
A Santander spokesman said that the November sale leaves the group with more than nine percent and less than 10 percent, a percentage that it will maintain on December 31.

"Banco Santander intends to retain a stake of more than nine percent in First Union, whose performance and outlook it views as highly favourable, while maintaining the shareholding below 10 percent so as to optimise the effect of the investment on group capital ratios," the statement said.
The sale was made at a price of $71-7/8 a share, realizing $151 million and resulting in a capital gain of $83 million for Banco Santander.
Santander said First Union had been informed of the transaction.
